detail.longDescription: # NativeNewsOnline Survey: Readers Oppose # DataCenters Near # TribalCommunities , Demand Tribal Say Survey finds # environmental concerns and # TribalSovereignty are central to readers’ views on data centers and # ArtificialIntelligence by Levi Rickert and Elyse Wild, October 22, 2026 PALM SPRINGS, Calif. — "Ahead of the 2026 # MidtermElections , Native News Online conducted an online survey last week to gauge readers’ views on data centers and artificial intelligence (AI). "Across the country, data centers and AI have become hot-button issues in the midterm elections. These issues are meaningful to Native News Online readers as well. Among those who took the survey, 77% said data centers and AI are important when evaluating candidates’ positions on issues. "In response to a question about whether they support data centers on or near their tribal communities, 75% of respondents said they are opposed. "The Native News Online survey results were consistent with responses to a national survey conducted September 11–14, 2026, by Beacon Research and Shaw & Company Research. That survey found that 71% of respondents opposed building AI data centers in their area, with 46% strongly opposed, while just 52% favored locating them in remote areas. "Among those who took the Native News Online survey, 91% said tribal nations should have a great deal of say in decisions about data centers or AI projects that could affect their lands, # NaturalResources , data or communities, including the ability to withhold consent when # TribalRights are affected. Another 7% said tribes should have a great deal of say through tribal consultation and formal agreements. "Water consumption, # EnergyUse , and # EnvironmentalImpact are the biggest concerns respondents have about data centers. 70% said they feel very negatively about the growing development of data centers in the U.S. 41% said they are familiar with the role of data centers in powering AI tools and other digital services. When asked how they feel about the growing use of AI in everyday life, 56.9% said they feel very negative, with 6% saying they feel very positive. "In response to a question asking respondents to identify any benefits, if any, of AI for Native people and tribal nations, 40.7% said education and research, 38.1% said health care and health research, and 30.1% said tribal language preservation. Among those who took the survey, the primary concerns about AI are misrepresentation of # NativePeoples and cultures; misuse or exploitation of # IndigenousKnowledge , stories, and cultural materials; and threats to privacy and tribal # DataSovereignty ." https:// nativenewsonline.net/currents/ native-news-online-survey-readers-oppose-data-centers-near-tribal-communities-demand-tribal-say/ # IndigenousSovereignty # EnvironmentalRacism # NoAIDatacenters # NoDatacentres # AirIsLife # WaterIsLife # LandIsLife # NoisePollution # AirPollution # AI # USPol # USElections # MidtermElections
